timeline.text: Checking the config, the trusted source, Kane and the budget.
Starting a fresh copy of the app with the trusted source loaded.
Kane is opening the source workspace and clicking Export.
Kane export: passed, exported the payments CSV on the Chicago payments page
Kane is creating an empty workspace to restore into.
Kane create-destination: passed, created a workspace on the local workspace site
Kane is uploading the exported file into the empty workspace.
Kane restore: passed, imported a CSV file on the workspace page
Kane is exporting the restored workspace.
Kane reexport: passed, downloaded the payments CSV on the payments page
Comparing every record against the trusted source.
source to export: All 1,000 of 1,000 rows came back unchanged
export to reexport: 1,000 of 1,000 rows came back, but department_name changed in 1,000 rows and vendor_name in 1,000 rows
source to reexport: 1,000 of 1,000 rows came back, but department_name changed in 1,000 rows and vendor_name in 1,000 rows
DATA_MISMATCH: 1,000 of 1,000 rows came back, but department_name changed in 1,000 rows and vendor_name in 1,000 rows

limitations: It proves the declared fields survive one CSV export, restore and re-export on a test copy of the app. It does not certify backups or fields outside the contract.
Kane uploads the restore file to TestMu AI cloud storage before setting it on the file input. Use public or test data only.
Kane drives the browser and reports its own pass or fail. ReturnTrip decides data equality with deterministic code and never trusts a browser success toast.
Controlled defects are recreated on a demo app and labelled as such. They are not a blind benchmark.
